message: In the DC vapour-compression cold room (C1), Maya, the pull-down of 1 tonne loaded hot has large one-day energy. To check it I used hand calculation (the 25 kWh pull-down thermal energy (E1)). I found 25 kWh thermal, about 10 kWh electric at Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling divided by electricity) 2.5, according to the JSDEWES solar refrigerator study reporting COP 2.75-3.02. I propose staged harvest intake plus ice-bank thermal storage. My position: not ready because night autonomy is not closed. In the tilted roof Photovoltaic array (PV, electricity from sunlight) with Maximum Power Point Tracking controller (MPPT, electronics that hold panels at peak power) (C2), Sam, the array size has risk of undersupply on cloudy days. To check it I used standard off-grid sizing with the sketch layout (the solar cold store layout (E2)). I found about 8-15 kWh per day steady load needs roughly 2-3 kW PV at 5 Peak Sun Hours with 25 percent losses, according to the ShopSolarKits off-grid sizing guide. I propose 3 kW tilted roof PV with south orientation. My position: not ready because battery size must be fixed first. In the 48V Lithium Iron Phosphate battery bank (LiFePO4, long-life lithium chemistry) (C3), colleagues, the night load has deep-discharge risk without diesel backup. To check it I used vendor cycle-life data with my pull-down estimate (the 25 kWh pull-down thermal energy (E1)).
